correctness.rationale: The root is uniquely positive by strict convexity of F; exact product telescoping matches the first support-interior midpoint. For integer r, strict Cauchy-Schwarz makes R(x) strictly decreasing, so h_a curvature changes sign at most once from negative to positive. The forward-difference derivative inherits this one-change pattern, proving k=2 controls all k≥2. The two strict comparison indices follow from the sign of h_a second derivative and the asymptotic constant from a uniform fixed-c Taylor expansion and harmonic sums. No numerical test stands in for infinite claims.

value.rationale: The family is explicitly used to illustrate discrete α-concavity in the source; its maximal parameter is an intrinsic and previously unspecified exact invariant. Identifying the first interior midpoint as universally decisive solves infinitely many constraints, gives strict improvement for all integer shapes, and an asymptotically nonvanishing gap. It yields a materially stronger applicability coefficient for the source variance inequality at shape r=3, while the paper makes no claim of optimality of that separate inequality.
